Its edge: it changes no gate, no record shape and nothing a session writes; it does not repair SEEN-006's R-04 (reworded in every field, a SEEN-145 residue of another kind); it does not rewrite any delivered kpi.json; and it moves no figure in any committed journal.

Evidence: a RED in harness/tests/test_calibration.py that builds record 1 = [F1 (c1, s1), F2 (c2, s2)] and record 2 = [G1 (c1, s2), G2 (c3, s1)], all at one file and line, and asserts kpi.findings sums to 2 over all four permutations (both orders of each record). Reproduced at clarify against HEAD d0c03e6: [G1, G2] gives 3 and [G2, G1] gives 2, so the RED fails today for the stated reason in at least one permutation.

2. For any two records of up to four findings each, from a small alphabet of claims, scenarios and lines, the count does not depend on the order of either record. Evidence: a property test that enumerates or draws (from a fixed seed, so no randomness unfaked, SEEN-136) record pairs over that alphabet, and for each pair asserts the count is the same under every permutation of both records. It must fail against today's greedy join, which the crossing case guarantees if the alphabet contains it.

4. SEEN-145's residue sentence goes, and the docstrings say what is maximised. Evidence: the diff removes the crossing-tie residue from kpi.findings' docstring and from the per-record comment in finding_identities, and finding_identities' docstring states what the assignment maximises and in which order (see decisions). SEEN-006's R-04 residue sentence stays, because this ticket does not touch it.
decisions: Stdlib only. The harness imports nothing outside the standard library (checked at clarify: hypothesis and scipy are not installed and no harness module imports a third-party package), so the assignment is written in harness/calibration.py rather than taken from scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment, and the property test of criterion 2 is an enumeration or a fixed-seed draw in unittest rather than a hypothesis strategy. Taken on the repository's existing practice; no new dependency is a scope this ticket does not have.

What is maximised, in order: first the number of joins this record makes (each join removes one identity from the count, which is the figure the ticket protects), then the summed strength of the joins under SEEN-145's ranking (texts shared, then the same file reference with its line, then the same id). Cardinality before weight, because a heavier assignment that places fewer findings is exactly the stranding the ticket removes. Reading of the ticket's 'maximises what is placed... weighted by the same ranking'; recorded here so the solution does not reopen it.

The final tie-break must not be position. Two assignments equal on count and weight can still build different identities, which later records join against, so a tie broken by list position could move a count one record later. The solution stage breaks the remaining tie on what the findings say (their texts, file and id), so findings with identical content are interchangeable and any others are ordered by content, and position is never read.

How the matching and the transitive merge compose is settled at solution, as the ticket says, with this observation already established: an identity holds at most one finding of a record (the join refuses two identities sharing a record), but one later finding may join several earlier identities that share no record, which is the merge. With only two records every earlier identity sits in record 1, so no later finding can ever join two of them: criterion 2's two-record property test cannot see the merge at all. The solution record therefore names a three-record test of the merge (an F in record 1 and an H in record 2 that do not match each other, joined by a G in record 3 that carries F's claim and H's scenario) besides the existing transitive cases, and states whether the merge step is optimised with the matching or after it.

Real journals keep their figures: SEEN-145's measured identities at clarify are unchanged by any assignment rule that agrees with the greedy join where the greedy join had no tie, and criterion 3's test is the observation that settles it for every committed journal.
No delegation at clarify: the questions were answered from the ticket, SEEN-145's notes 36, 44 and 55, the code at harness/calibration.py:272-366 and one measurement script, each one call.
